newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Hughes, GM firmer.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Hughes, GM firmer.

text.p: Shares in Hughes Electronics Corp and its parent company General Motors Corp traded higher preceding Friday's market open after GM announced the sale of Hughes Aircraft to Raytheon Co for $9.5 billion in stock and debt.
Before the open, Hughes rose 1/4 to 63 while GM climbed to 61-1/2 from 60-3/8, traders said.
Neither Raytheon nor Northrop Grumman Corp, which lost in the bidding for the GM's defense business, made moves before the open.

Electronics for Imaging Inc shares were bought up in early trade on the appeal of fourth quarter results that exceeded Wall Street expectations. The shares rose to 91 from 88-1/2, according to traders.
After the market close last night, the company said it earned $0.73 per share in the three months ended December 31, $0.10 better than expected by securities analysts.
The company earned $0.46 one year ago.
C-Cube Microsystems Inc shed 1-7/8 to 37 after the company reported earnings of $0.45 per share after the market close last night.
The results exceeded Wall Street expectations by $0.01 per share, but failed to fulfill heightened expectations that drove the shares 3-7/8 higher in yesterday's Nasdaq trade.
Ascend Communications Inc stock climbed to 72 from 68-7/8 following a fourth quarter earnings report that surpassed analysts' expectations.
After the close last night, Ascend said it earned $0.32 per share, $0.01 better than the Wall Street estimate.
Also, Studio Plus Hotels Inc shares are expected to trade higher after Extended Stay America said it will acquire Studio Plus in a $290 million stock-swap.
Before the open, Studio Plus shares were quoted at 15-1/2 bid, 16-1/2 ask, above last night's 14-3/4 close.
The companies said each Studio Plus share will be swapped for 1.2272 Extended Stay shares, worth about $$22.85 based on Thursday closing prices.
